correctness.rationale: Under tie-free common null the binary word is uniform among binom(N,m) fixed-composition words. At pooled rank j, F_m−G_n=B_j/(mn), H_N has jumps 1/N, so T=ΣB_j²/(mnN²). Hypergeometric variance yields E B_j²=mn j(N−j)/(N−1), summing E S=mnN(N+1)/6. R=1+Σ I_i. P(I_i=1)=2mn/[N(N−1)]. Condition on one adjacent transition: two distinguished positions contain one label each with equally likely orientations, remaining N−2 positions a uniform (m−1,n−1) word. Case j<i, j=i, j>i conditional means/variances give Σ_i E[S|I_i=1]=N(N−1)[(N−1)mn+N]/6; inserting into Σ_iCov(I_i,S) gives −mn(2mn−N)/3. Handle N=2,3 by enumeration. Independent exact Fraction exhaustive all compositions 2≤N≤11 matched formula, source verifier additionally checks 8,166 binary words through N12 and 777 conditional identities through N40. Algebra supplies all N, not finite extrapolation. For N≥3, mn≥N−1 ensures negativity; limit follows directly.

value.rationale: The Wald–Wolfowitz runs test counts local rank alternations while Cramér–von Mises integrates the global squared two-sample empirical bridge. Their exact mixed null covariance is a motivated dependence/calibration statistic, with universal strict negative sign and nonzero proportional-sample limit. Neither marginal null law computes the coupling; not an arbitrary small parameter slice.

final_claim: For two samples m,n≥1 from the same continuous law (N=m+n), the pooled rank-label run count R and T=(mn/N)∫(F_m−G_n)^2 dH_N satisfy exact Cov(R,T)=−(2mn−N)/(3N²), zero only for m=n=1 and negative for N≥3. Equivalently Cov(R,Σ_{j=1}^{N−1}(N A_j−mj)²)=−mn(2mn−N)/3; proportional m/N→λ∈(0,1) yields −2λ(1−λ)/3.
